name: Vehicle Routing with Time-Dependent Travel Times benchmarks
description: We develop theoretical foundations and practical algorithms for vehicle routing with time-dependent travel times. We also provide new benchmark instances and experimental results. First, we study basic operations on piecewise linear arrival time functions. In particular, we devise a faster algorithm to compute the pointwise minimum of a set of piecewise linear functions and a monotonicity-preserving variant of the Imai-Iri algorithm to approximate an arrival time function with fewer breakpoints. Next, we show how to evaluate insertion and deletion operations in tours efficiently and update the underlying data structure faster than previously known when a tour changes. Evaluating a tour also requires a scheduling step which is non-trivial in the presence of time windows and time-dependent travel times. We show how to perform this in linear time. Based on these results, we develop a local search heuristic to solve real-world vehicle routing problems with various constraints efficiently a
reputation: A specialized research benchmark used in vehicle routing and operations research, but not broadly adopted outside that community.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark with instance-specific optimization objectives; scores depend on problem constraints and are not directly comparable across datasets.
